newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index up on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index up on foreign demand.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index continued its upward trend on Wednesday, rising for a third straight day on demand from foreign investors, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index gained 11.73 points to stand at 3024.40.

Activity on the foreign board accounted for about 68 percent of the total turnover in the market. Turnover was a record 35.394 million shillings on trade of 1,087,600 shares, versus 24.178 million shillings on Tuesday. Tuesday's turnover was the highest the market had seen over the last two weeks.

Some 704,000 shares of Firestone East Africa were traded on the three-day-offer board at a reserve price of 30, while 20,900 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank were traded at between 58.50-59 from 57.50.
Some 5,600 shares of Kakuzi were traded at 97.50 from 97 while 7,200 shares of Kenya Breweries were traded at between 50-50.50 versus 50.

"The interest shown by foreigners in our market reflects the confidence they have in our market. A lot of them are finding it more profitable to invest in emerging markets all over the world," a broker said.
Many brokers, however, were uncertain the trend would continue.
"To be honest, we're still in a limbo. There's no sign that that the upsurge will be sustained. People are hesitant because they don't know what direction the market will take," a senior broker said.

Agriculturals, a traditional favourite of institutional investors, recorded marginal improvements in price. Brooke Bond moved to close at 178 from 174, while George Williamson Kenya gained two to close at 72.
